title: Wells Fargo Resets S&P 500 Target With a Catch - TradingView
text: Wells Fargo Resets S&P 500 Target With a Catch 1 min read SPX Wells Fargo has cut its year-end S&P 500 target to 7,700 from 7,950, warning that investors are entering the late stages of the market's growth cycle just as political risks and pressure on technology stocks complicate the outlook. The revised target implies only about 1% upside from the index's recent 7,619.98 close, signaling that the bank sees limited room for further gains through the rest of 2026 despite strong corporate earnings. The S&P 500 has still gained 11.3% this year, weathering Middle East tensions, sticky inflation and periodic volatility. Corporate fundamentals also remain resilient. Roughly 85.7% of S&P 500 companies reporting second-quarter results beat Wall Street earnings estimates. Wells Fargo is not turning outright bearish on profits. The bank actually raised its S&P 500 earnings-per-share forecast to $425 for 2027 and $460 for 2028. The concern is what investors will be willing to pay for those earnings. Wells Fargo said the market is moving deeper into a late-cycle environment, where valuation multiples typically compress and price gains become harder to generate. The bank also warned that its 2028 earnings forecast could prove too optimistic if major technology companies pull back on massive AI infrastructure spending. That risk is already changing its sector positioning. Wells Fargo downgraded U.S. technology stocks to equal weight from overweight following Monday's AI-led selloff and rising political pushback against large data-center developments ahead of the midterm elections. At the same time, the bank upgraded healthcare to overweight from equal weight as a more defensive late-cycle opportunity. Investors Takeaway Wells Fargo's call suggests the next leg of the market may depend less on earnings growth and more on valuation. Investors should watch AI capital spending, tech earnings revisions and whether political pressure begins delaying data-center projects. A sustained slowdown in hyperscaler spending would threaten both tech valuations and Wells Fargo's longer-term earnings assumptions. Conversely, continued strong earnings combined with resilient AI investment could make the 7,700 target look conservative. For now, Wells Fargo's shift toward healthcare signals a preference for earnings durability over chasing further tech multiple expansion.
